parent_release: Get Close (Real Records/Sire Records), Oct. 20, 1986 (UK), Nov. 4, 1986 (US)
info: Chrissie Hynde wrote the song, and Jimmy Iovine produced it, with Bob Clearmountain mixing. It was the lead single from Get Close and reached No. 10 on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the UK Singles Chart. Hynde has said she wrote it for her friend, tennis player John McEnroe.
flags: Single date differs by market: Wikidata gives Aug. 5, 1986 (UK) and Sept. 23, 1986 (US, Sire 7-28630); one site says Sept. 22. The album, not the single, is the Oct. 20, 1986 UK release in the plan. Check Discogs if an exact UK day matters.

info: Will Toledo of Car Seat Headrest produced and recorded Midnight, and he sings this song as a duet with Chura and plays guitar, bass, synth and piano on it. It is the tenth track on her second album. Chura has said the chorus and guitar riff came after the unexpected death of a close friend.
flags: Single date of May 15, 2019 comes from the YouTube audio upload and same-day press coverage; Bandcamp lists the track at the album date, June 7, 2019. Use June 7, 2019 if the single date is not wanted.

info: Sub Pop issued it as a 7-inch single with "The Snake of Addis Ababa" ahead of the album, and a video directed by Henrik Nyblom and Christofer Hogberg followed. Requiem is the Swedish band's third studio album, released in North America by Sub Pop and elsewhere by Rocket Recordings. The track is built on mostly acoustic instruments.
flags: Exact single day not confirmed: Sub Pop video post is dated May 9, 2016 and a SoundCloud/YouTube upload shows 5/27/16. Album date Oct. 7, 2016 is confirmed by Sub Pop and Bandcamp.

info: "Sandy" is a track on the Los Angeles band's self-titled debut album. Nick Waterhouse produced the record, and it came out on his Innovative Leisure label. The band's members met while working at Amoeba Records in Los Angeles.
flags: Wikipedia gives only September 2012; Rate Your Music, Album of the Year and a retailer give Sept. 18.

track: Walk to the One You Love
parent_release: Down in Heaven (Grand Jury Music), May 13, 2016
info: It was the lead single and opening track of the Chicago band's third album, Down in Heaven. The track was produced by Twin Peaks and R. Andrew Humphrey and mixed by John Agnello, with Will Miller on flugelhorn. The video is a single continuous tracking shot through a Chicago neighborhood.
flags: Feb. 1, 2016 is the Bandcamp track date; press coverage of the announcement and single is from February 2016.

info: "Doorway" opens bitknot, the band's third album, released on Saddle Creek. The album came as a surprise release at the label's suggestion, according to the band, and Lydia Slocum sings lead. Slocum and Kinsler have named this song as one of their favorites on the record.
flags: Digital date May 26, 2026 agrees across sources. Physical release date differs (Saddle Creek lists June 26, Bandcamp lists Nov. 6, 2026).

info: The Vancouver band released it as the first single from Pray 4 Tomorrow, its third LP for Mint Records. The band wrote and produced the album, and Nick Short recorded and mixed it at CHOMS studio. Members are Franco Rossino, Shelby Vredik, Pipe Morelli and Nick Short.
flags: Northern Transmissions gives Nov. 4, 2022 for the album; Mint Records, Bandcamp and Stereogum say Nov. 11.

info: "The End" is the opening track of Highway to Hell, the Star Moles album from Emily Moales. It was recorded, mixed and mastered by Kevin Basko at Historic New Jersey in 2025, and the label of the same name released it. Reviewers describe the opener as piano-driven.
flags: A UK retailer (Pie & Vinyl) lists Dec. 4, 2026, probably a later vinyl edition; every other source gives Feb. 26, 2026.

info: "The Clue" opens the five-track EP Hive, Vol. 2, which runs about 1:39 for this song. Buz Clatworthy wrote and recorded everything at Frog House Studios, and he and Beau Langdon mixed it at Big Time Studios. The EP is catalog number WART010 on Warttmann Inc.
flags: Label confirmed as Warttmann Inc. on its own Bandcamp page (WART010). Shazam credits Anti Fade Records, which looks wrong.

track: Never Like You Said (feat. Courtney Barnett)
parent_release: Bocca di Lupo (Sacred Bones Records), Nov. 6, 2026
info: It was the first single from the duo's two companion albums, Bocca di Lupo and Mouth of the Wolf, both out Nov. 6 on Sacred Bones. Barnett sings on the second track of Bocca di Lupo, with words the duo says were improvised in the studio. Both albums were recorded in July 2025 at Fonoprint Studios in Bologna, on Via Bocca di Lupo.
flags: Single date Sept. 9, 2026 came from a search summary; the coverage is dated September 2026 but the exact day should be checked against the Stereogum or Consequence post.

info: A cover of George Michael's "Careless Whisper," which Michael wrote with Andrew Ridgeley and released in 1984 (on Wham!'s Make It Big). Jesse Hughes, performing as Boots Electric, recorded it for a covers album of 13 songs he wished he had written, released by UMe. This version drops the original's saxophone line.
flags: Label shown as UMe (Universal Music Enterprises), per the band's own announcement; Universal is correct.

info: A standalone single on City Slang, not tied to an album. The band's most recent album was Who Let the Dogs Out in 2025. The video was directed by Harv Frost.
flags: Date of March 31, 2026 comes from streaming listings (Apple, Amazon); the press articles were not checked for the day.

info: It is the second single from the band's ninth album, Perfecth, after "Easy Street," and the second track on the album. Josh Homme and bassist Michael Shuman produced the album. Homme has called the song one about distance, and the band says the released version was its second take.
flags: Plan says Aug. 28, 2026. Matador's announcement says the song was out Aug. 25, 2026 with the album news; Spotify metadata reportedly shows Aug. 25 and Aug. 29, and The Obelisk post is dated Aug. 28.
